sub_answers.sub_question: What disputes arose over representation of Bosnia's ethnic groups within the national team and football association?
sub_answers.text: Football in Bosnia split along ethnic lines with Bosnian Croats forming the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and a Croat-only First League in 1993 and Bosnian Serbs organising the First League of the Republika Srpska in 1993, creating separate representation pathways outside the N/FSBiH [d55965203s4p0]. The national competitions were therefore divided territorially and ethnically, while football under the N/FSBiH operated mainly in areas controlled by Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina institutions and had a Bosniak majority influence [d55965203s4p0]. Ethnic nationalism between Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs underpinned these divisions and competing claims over statehood and representation in Bosnia and Herzegovina more broadly [d63104390s1p0].

sub_answers.text: No official domestic league matches were played in the 1992–93 season due to the outbreak of the Bosnian War, disrupting football activity nationwide [d55965203s4p0]. In late 1993 some parts of the country re-launched football competitions but only with reduced scope and largely confined to ethnically controlled areas, limiting national-level organisation and development [d55965203s4p0]. Competition under N/FSBiH auspices largely stood down until the 1995–96 season when the Bosnian First League officially resumed, causing a multi-year interruption to formal national football structures [d55965203s4p0].

sub_answers.text: During and after the breakup of Yugoslavia football in Bosnia and Herzegovina was divided along ethnic lines, producing separate Croat, Serb and Bosniak spheres of competition rather than a unified national structure [d55965203s4p0]. In 1993 Bosnian Croats launched the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and a Croat-only First League of Herzeg-Bosnia, restricting Croat clubs to a parochial competition [d55965203s4p0]. In the same year Bosnian Serbs organized the First League of the Republika Srpska on territory held by the Republika Srpska regime, separating Serb clubs from N/FSBiH competitions [d55965203s4p0]. Football remaining under the auspices of the N/FSBiH was effectively under institutions with a Bosniak majority during the war period, creating an imbalance in control and representation [d55965203s4p0].
